new_task_1.title: Restore PyPI search result parsing for current search-page markup
new_task_1.description: Poetry 1.6.0 replaces the brittle html5lib/XPath scraping used for PyPI searches with a dedicated HTML parser that matches PyPI's current `package-snippet` markup. PyPI-backed search results can once again yield package names, versions, and descriptions even when the page uses nested span elements or multi-token class attributes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that PyPI search results are parsed correctly from the current `pypi.org/search` HTML so package lookup features continue to return usable package names, versions, and descriptions instead of silently missing results because the page markup no longer matches the old scraper.

expectation.grounded: `PyPiRepository.search` should fetch the PyPI search page, feed `response.text` into `SearchResultParser`, recognize result anchors whose class list contains `package-snippet`, extract the package name from `span.package-snippet__name`, the version from `span.package-snippet__version`, and the description from `p.package-snippet__description`, then build `Package` objects from those parsed values. Parsed descriptions should be stripped before assignment, and entries with invalid versions should continue to be skipped.
expectation.conceptual: Search features that rely on PyPI's HTML results should remain functional after PyPI markup changes, returning real package search hits instead of failing because the parser depended on an older DOM shape or exact class-attribute strings.

constraints.grounded: Only results that provide both a parsed name and version should be added. Description text remains optional and should default to an empty string when absent. Existing invalid-version handling must remain non-fatal: malformed versions are skipped rather than aborting the full search result set. The parser must match relevant CSS classes by token presence rather than by exact full-string equality.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the scope narrow to search-result extraction. The fix should make PyPI search robust to the current page structure without changing unrelated repository lookup or package validation behavior.

behavior: PyPI search result parsing recognizes package snippets based on CSS class membership instead of exact class-string matches.
For each recognized result snippet, Poetry extracts the package name, version, and description from the current nested HTML structure.
Search result descriptions are trimmed before being stored on the resulting package objects.
Entries whose versions cannot be parsed continue to be skipped without failing the overall search.
acceptance_criteria: When the PyPI search page contains result anchors marked with the `package-snippet` class and nested `package-snippet__name` and `package-snippet__version` spans, the search operation should return packages with those names and versions.
When a result snippet includes a `package-snippet__description` paragraph with surrounding whitespace, the returned package description should contain the trimmed text.
When a result snippet omits either the name or version field, that incomplete snippet should not be emitted as a package result.
When a result snippet contains an invalid version string, the search operation should skip that entry and continue returning the other valid results.
When relevant class attributes include additional CSS class tokens beyond the expected one, the parser should still recognize the result so long as the required class token is present.
